newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK February producer price data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK February producer price data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK producer price data showing input prices falling 6.6 percent year-on-year and annual output price inflation of 1.3 percent.

"Inflation data, as expected, obviously very tame at the moment. Food prices and energy prices have obviously come down somewhat, reflecting better weather and the strength of sterling. On balance, the data are pretty much what we expected."

"An almost total lack of inflationary pressures in the manufacturing sector. The fall in input prices reflects the strength of sterling and maybe falling oil prices too. The Bank of England Governor will continue to argue for a small monetary tightening but we do detect that his tone has softened over the last few weeks. The critical factor now is the extent to which weak producer prices feed through into retail prices."

"Relative to the market consensus these numbers were good, especially on the input price side...we got a substantially bigger reduction in manufacturers' costs than was generally expected. That's a reflection of the big drop in oil prices we saw last month."

"The market expected some pretty good figures but the June gilt contract could recover towards 112-16 this week. Short sterling also looks like it will push higher towards 93.70 in the June contract. Everything points towards a very low interest rate environment irrespective of whether we've got an election or not. We might see a bit of a wobble in sterling, maybe down as low as 1.57 against the U.S. dollar."
